$comment: EBU R 128 s1 is the short-form envelope: R 128 recommends (q) delegates adverts, promos and similar items here, and s1 states a tolerance and a Maximum Short-term Loudness that plain R 128 does not. Keeping the two apart is the point — a ±0.2 LU tolerance read off a commercials spec is s1's QC allowance, not a house tightening of programme R 128, and must not leak into a programme profile.
name: EBU R 128 s1

document.title: EBU R 128 s1 — Loudness Parameters for Short-form Content (Adverts; Promos etc.)

assets.audio.loudness.standards[].target.quote: that the Programme Loudness Level shall be normalised to a Target Level of −23.0 LUFS. For the implementation of Loudness workflows (for example, in Quality Control environments) a tolerance of ±0.2 LU is allowed in order to take account of measurement errors;
assets.audio.loudness.standards[].target.note: Same constant as programme R 128 — short-form content is normalised to the same target; only the tolerance and the short-term ceiling differ.

assets.audio.loudness.standards[].tolera.quote: For the implementation of Loudness workflows (for example, in Quality Control environments) a tolerance of ±0.2 LU is allowed in order to take account of measurement errors;
assets.audio.loudness.standards[].tolera.note: s1 carries no equivalent of R 128 (h)'s ±1.0 LU live exception — short-form content is not live, so the QC measurement allowance is the whole of the tolerance. A short-form spec at ±1.0 LU is looser than the standard it names.

assets.audio.loudness.true_peak_max.quote: and that the True Peak Level of the programme shall not exceed −1 dBTP (dB True Peak) for linear audio, measured with a meter compliant with ITU-R BS.1770 and EBU Tech 3341. The measurement tolerance is ±0.3 dB (for signals with a bandwidth limited to 20 kHz).
assets.audio.loudness.true_peak_max.note: Footnote 1 refers the reader to EBU Tech 3344 for Maximum Permitted True Peak Levels on different distribution systems, i.e. a lower ceiling is expected for coded delivery.

assets.audio.loudness.short_term_max.quote: that the Short-term Loudness Level (measured in compliance with EBU Tech 3341) shall not exceed −18.0 LUFS (+5.0 LU on the relative scale). For the implementation of loudness workflows (for example, in Quality Control environments) a tolerance of +0.2 LU is allowed in order to take account of measurement errors;
assets.audio.loudness.short_term_max.note: Bounded, not locked: −18.0 LUFS is the loosest ceiling s1 permits and a spec may sit lower — the same directional rule as true_peak_max. Plain R 128 states no short-term ceiling at all, so this constraint belongs to the short-form content class alone; a programme profile carrying one is stating a house limit, not R 128. Note also that the QC allowance here is one-sided (+0.2 LU on a ceiling), unlike the ±0.2 LU two-sided tolerance on the target.

assets.audio.loudness.standards[].lra_ma.cite: clause 'The measure Loudness Range is not useful for short-form content'
assets.audio.loudness.standards[].lra_ma.quote: The measure 'Loudness Range' is not useful for short-form content. It is based on a statistical analysis of the Short-term (3 s) Loudness values. For commercials, promos etc. this leaves too few data points for a meaningful result. Therefore, a maximum and/or minimum value for Loudness Range shall not be specified for programmes of this length/genre.
assets.audio.loudness.standards[].lra_ma.note: Not merely unset — s1 says a value shall not be specified at all, so an LRA ceiling on a short-form profile contradicts the standard it names.
